solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Travel first class? Put yourself down for a saver!

parts.note: to travel is to go
A is the top grade, first class
to lie is to put yourself down flat

explanation.surface: A travel advert urging you to go first class and sign up for a money-saving deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saver' reads as someone saving money; in football it is the player who makes saves. 'Put yourself down' reads as signing up, but it means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper's whole job is making saves, so a keeper can be called a saver.

clue.text: Party drink to sink after picking up a snail?

definitions.note: a snail is one example of the class

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it, so the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a do is a party
port is a fortified wine
to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: Someone at a party slumping with a drink after picking up a snail.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces are strung together and the whole string is then turned upwards; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails belong to the mollusc class of gastropods, so a snail is one example of the group.

clue.text: Pick out dhal, oddly passing up bean

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from the bottom to the top
the odd-numbered letters pass away, leaving only the even-numbered ones behind

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Someone picking the beans out of a dish of dhal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick out' looks like the instruction, but it is simply part of the letter string; 'oddly passing' drops every odd letter of that string.
explanation.definitionFit: The aduki is a small red bean used in Asian cooking, much like the pulses in dhal.

clue.text: Knowledge largely hard to find by day? None of us can see it

definitions.text: None of us can see it

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: info is short for information, knowledge
something rare is hard to find
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A riddle about some knowledge so obscure that nobody can see it by daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by day' reads as 'in daylight', but 'by' just places D next to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared radiation lies beyond the red end of the visible spectrum, so human eyes cannot detect it.

clue.text: Time, with very large middle, to get XL!

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
W is the abbreviation for with
OS is outsize, the clothing size for very large
the core is the middle of something

explanation.surface: Time and a big middle-aged spread push you up to an extra-large clothing size.
explanation.walkthrough: XL looks like the clothing size, but it is the Roman numeral for forty.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so two of them make forty, which Roman numerals write as XL.

clue.text: City to have Liberal MP worn out!

indicators.note: something knocked out of shape has lost its form, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city is lumbered with an exhausted Liberal Member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn out' reads as one phrase meaning tired; 'worn' is fodder and 'out' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolverhampton is a city in the English West Midlands, near Birmingham.

clue.text: Figure in charge, still

parts.note: a stat, statistic, is a figure
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a figure is still in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a person or a shape; here it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Something static is not moving, the same as the adjective still.

clue.text: New lad alone, somehow not missing anybody

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged into another order

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new boy on his own somehow doesn't miss anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a lonely lad; the definition is the phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everybody without exception, so nobody at all is left out.

clue.text: Overreact when volume turned up close to one

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means flipped to read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a tome is a large book, a volume

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of one

explanation.surface: Someone overreacts when the volume on the stereo is turned up to near maximum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' and 'turned up' suggest sound level; the volume is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to express feelings theatrically, which is what overacting or overreacting amounts to.

clue.text: Fail with things at college

parts.note: stuff means things, possessions
in British usage a student is up at university

explanation.surface: A student failing with all their belongings at college.
explanation.walkthrough: British students go up to university and are then up there, so 'at college' gives UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff up is informal for to bungle or mess things up, so to fail at a task.

clue.text: For energy, helping to provide a great deal

definitions.note: noun phrase for a large quantity

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
life means vitality or energy
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: A pitch for energy suppliers who promise to provide a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' reads as a verb, assisting, but it is a noun: a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A proliferation is a rapid increase to large numbers, hence an abundance or great amount.

clue.text: Drop round, in pursuit of meadow plant, for dinner?

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the first item named comes after the rest

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
veg is a plant eaten at dinner
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An invitation to drop round for dinner after gathering meadow plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop round' reads as one phrase, pop in; 'Drop' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave go is an informal British way of saying let go, so to release your grip.

clue.text: Girl to be educated earlier retaking a course in India

indicators.note: taking something in again means holding it inside

parts.note: Educating Rita is a 1980 play about a woman who goes back to study
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mature student returning to take a course in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a Willy Russell play and film; 'course' reads as a study course but is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt side dish served with Indian meals, so it is one course or part of the meal.

clue.text: Be done with ice breaking and falling in?

indicators.note: something breaking comes apart, and its pieces are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A skater finished off when the ice breaks and they fall into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling in' pictures a plunge through ice; it also means falling into line, lining up as ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who fall in are obeying the order to form ranks, so compliance is shown.

clue.text: One offering purse with fancy zip — her gift?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborately made up, so the letters are dressed up into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A present of a handbag with a smart zip, wondering if it is her gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purse' reads as a handbag; in boxing the purse is the prize money for a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional boxing match is fought for a purse, the money awarded to the fighters.

clue.text: Wrong being at home with no lemon wedge?

parts.note: someone at home is in
a drink with ice only and no lemon wedge comes with just ice

explanation.surface: Feeling hard done by at home because the drink came without its lemon slice.
explanation.walkthrough: The bartender's question is 'ice and a slice?'; without the slice you get just ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An injustice is an unfair act, a wrong done to someone.

clue.text: Collected monies originally given by state

indicators.note: one thing given by another is placed beside it

parts.note: Cal is short for California, a US state

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of monies

explanation.surface: Tax money gathered in and handed out by the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collected' reads as gathered in; it is the adjective meaning composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cool and collected is composed and unruffled, which is being calm.

clue.text: No reason not to be miles up indeed in a balloon!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means at the top, so this item heads the column

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for miles
ay is an old form of yes, indeed
taken as written
to balloon is to swell up

explanation.surface: A balloonist reasoning that there is no harm in floating miles up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balloon' reads as the hot-air craft; it is a verb meaning to swell.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a shrug meaning there is nothing to lose by doing something, so there is no reason against it.

clue.text: Mostly lacking knowledge about current matter as a whole

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the final letter goes
about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: unversed means not knowledgeable; its last letter is dropped
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone ignorant about current affairs, the whole issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current matter' reads as topical affairs; current is electrical, and 'matter as a whole' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is all existing matter and space considered together, the cosmos.

clue.text: One of two discs moved inside record player, making room for karate?

indicators.note: shifting something inside places it within another piece

parts.note: a DJ plays records
each O is disc-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone moves a record deck to make room for karate practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record player' reads as a turntable; it is the disc jockey. The two Os follow DJ, then one of them is moved inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dojo is a training hall for martial arts such as karate or judo.

clue.text: Room in a box is restricting, extremely

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: the box and the telly are British slang for television
RM is the abbreviation for room
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Complaining that a room inside a box is terribly cramped.
explanation.walkthrough: Telly is British slang for television, as is 'the box'.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminally is used informally as an intensifier, as in terminally dull, meaning to an extreme degree.

clue.text: One visiting sailor, lover of pop perhaps and heavy metal

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so this piece enters another

parts.note: pop is dad, and his partner is mum
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A visiting sailor who loves pop music and heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' and 'heavy metal' read as music genres; pop is father, and heavy metal is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring chemical element, a very heavy metal.

clue.text: Begin by shoving hard to stop cat biting

indicators.note: a stopper is plugged into an opening, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: puss is a cat
H is the pencil grade for hard
tart means sharp or biting in taste or tone

explanation.surface: Pushing hard to stop a cat from biting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' reads as a cat's action; it is an adjective meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: To push-start a car is to get its engine going by shoving it along, so to begin it by pushing.

clue.text: Montgomery is in this year overwhelmed by war captives

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so it sits inside what surrounds it

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Field Marshal Montgomery this year surrounded by prisoners of war.
explanation.walkthrough: Montgomery suggests the wartime general; it is a small town in Powys, a county in mid-Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Powys is a Welsh county whose towns include Montgomery, which gave the old county of Montgomeryshire its name.

clue.text: Tools to get hold of instead of spades

parts.note: vice is Latin for in place of, as in vice-captain
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A gardener told to get hold of other tools instead of spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spades' look like garden tools, matching 'Tools'; they are the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a bench clamp with jaws that grips a workpiece firmly while you work on it.

clue.text: Press pipe down underneath vineyard

indicators.note: in a vertical entry, underneath means placed lower in the column, so this item comes second

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or wine growth
sh is the call to be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone in the press told to pipe down while at a vineyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests journalists or a wine press; it is the verb, squash.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush grapes is to press them hard to extract the juice, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Resort's website, editable without a single click, ultimately

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: a wiki is a website any user can edit
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of click

explanation.surface: A holiday resort's booking website that is editable without a single mouse click.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking; in the old sense it means outside, so the wiki wraps the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Waikiki is a famous beach resort district of Honolulu on the Hawaiian island of Oahu.

clue.text: Train in Peru trundling around

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters read right to left
the answer sits in the following words, spread across them

parts.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word to the seventh of the second

explanation.surface: A train rolling slowly around the Peruvian mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' reads as a railway train; it is the verb, to bring up or develop.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture someone is to raise and develop them, just as to train is to educate and form.

clue.text: Furious drunk committing crime on Tube?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: British slang for very intoxicated
third meaning: a gang rushing through a train carriage robbing passengers

explanation.surface: An angry drunk causing trouble on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses of one word; the Tube is the London Underground, where gangs once robbed passengers by charging through carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for both enraged and heavily intoxicated, and it names gang robbery on crowded trains.

clue.text: Making one pass on licence given to small boy

parts.note: a property let is rented out on licence
Hal is a short form of Henry

explanation.surface: A learner driver passing the test and getting a licence, handed to a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' and 'licence' suggest a driving test; 'pass' is to pass away, die.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lethal is deadly, causing a person to pass on or die.
